name: calm dark worn asphalt road in two close tones with sparse light aggregate, a long hairline crack, two different repair patches and an oil stain, its unconnected edges frayed into the dirt with bitten-out gaps and loose chunks instead of an outline, laid as a road network with crossroads and dead ends
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt

surfaces.part: dirt ground background with grey asphalt road patches (crossroads, dead ends, large repaired slab)

answer.evidence: This is a flat top-down terrain sheet. The silhouette is a full 256-wide rectangle on every row from 0 to 191. The road pieces are irregular dirt-edged patches with no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no vertical face and no ellipse. The column scans show only texture banding, with no front face. It is a flat ground texture, not a standing object, so it has no front face and no depth cues.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are fine: 5 visible tones per tile (grass reference 3, paving reference 7), 2% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edges. The edges are frayed with no outline, and the dirt has tinted speckle and chunk texture, so it is not a sticker and not flat. The weak point is ramp depth. The asphalt is essentially two close blue-grey tones plus a dark crack and stain, so about 3 steps. The dirt is about 3-4 brown steps, and the whole piece uses only 14 colours. The Beodeul references carry 5-6 steps per material. The asphalt has no per-chunk highlights or grain structure beyond a sparse speckle. The large right-hand patch is the only place the crack and oil stain appear. The two distinct repair patches are not readable, and the road pieces are small isolated blobs rather than a clear network. Compared with the references, it looks thinner and less crafted in its shading, so it does not clearly meet the bar.

surfaces.part: dirt ground with asphalt road patches (whole sheet)

answer.evidence: The sheet is a flat top-down terrain tile set. Rows 0-191 are fully opaque at width 256. The column scans show only alternating texture bands of dirt and asphalt, with no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no vertical south face. The road patches are flat grey-blue shapes with frayed edges on brown dirt, drawn as ground texture with no front face. This fits terrain, which is expected to be flat, so no front face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a ground patch, the same kind as the grass and paving references. Its asphalt has about 3 close slate tones, with speckled aggregate and mottling. The dirt around it has about 4-5 browns in clustered, scalloped grain. The measured facts sit between the two references: 5 visible tones per tile (grass 3, paving 7), 2% near-flat coverage (references 0%) and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. The edges are frayed into the dirt with bitten-out gaps and loose chunks, with no outline and no sticker look. The one large patch has a dark crack and oil stains. Two things count against it: the asphalt ramp is shallow, because the brief asks for two close tones, and the dirt blotches are somewhat repetitive. Even so, it is not flatter or thinner than the grass reference, and it is close to the paving reference in density. A careful artist would accept it next to the references.

surfaces.part: dirt ground base with asphalt road segments (crossroads, dead ends, patches, crack and oil stain)

answer.evidence: This is a flat, full-bleed terrain sheet, 256 px wide in every row from 0 to 191. It shows dirt with dark asphalt road shapes seen straight from above. The roads have frayed edges, a crack, patches and an oil stain, and the column scans show only texture variation. There is no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse, or vertical south face anywhere. Each column shows only alternating tone bands, which are texture and not a top plane over a front face. Since the tiles have no front face (0 rows), it is a top-down slab, which is expected for ground terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has no outline. The unconnected edges are frayed into the dirt with bitten gaps and loose chunks, which matches the Beodeul habit of separating forms by value alone. The measured facts support this: 0% neutral dark edge pixels, only 2% near-flat coverage, and 5 visible tones per tile. That sits between the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7). The asphalt is mottled with dark and light aggregate speckle in two close tones plus a darker crack and oil stain. The dirt carries about 3-4 brown tones with grain, so no large area reads as a flat fill. Only about 14 colours are used in total, and the asphalt ramp is shallow at roughly 3 steps, which is slightly below the 5-6 steps of Beodeul. That shallowness is largely intended by the 'two close tones' brief. Overall the piece would sit acceptably next to the references and does not look like a sticker.

surfaces.part: ground tile with road network (dirt base, road patches, crack, repair patches, oil stain)

answer.evidence: This is a flat top-down terrain tile. The silhouette is 256 px wide on every row from 0 to 191, so it is a full rectangle with no outline. The column scans show only mottled texture bands (dirt tones, crack and stain pixels) with no front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or vertical front face. The road segments are flat patches with frayed edges on a dirt ground, and no south face is drawn. For terrain this is expected: it reads as a top-down slab with no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The asphalt carries two close slate tones plus light aggregate flecks and dark crack and stain accents, so about 4 steps against the reference's 5-6. The dirt around it is dithered in several brown tones with pebble dots. Measured facts support this: 5 visible tones per tile sits between the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7), and near-flat coverage is only 2% against 0% for both references. There is no outline. The road edges are frayed into the dirt with bitten gaps and loose chunks, and the 0% near-neutral edge share confirms there is no neutral black line. The road network reads clearly, with crossroads, dead ends and a larger patch. The crack and oil stain are visible, though the two repair patches are hard to tell apart. The asphalt is somewhat tonally shallow but is intentionally calm and close-toned. It is textured, not a sticker, and holds up next to the references.
